  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `{"k": "a<TAB>b"}`, an object value | bytes `7b226b223a2022615c7462227d`, written back as its escape | `22P02`, `0x09` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `{"k": "a<LF>b"}`, an object value | bytes `7b226b223a2022615c6e62227d`, written back as its escape | `22P02`, `0x0a` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `{"k": "a<1F>b"}`, an object value | bytes `7b226b223a2022615c753030316662227d`, written back as a `\u` escape | `22P02`, `0x1f` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `{"a<01>b": 1}`, an object key | bytes `7b22610162223a20317d`, the character raw | `22P02`, `0x01` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `{"a<TAB>b": 1}`, an object key | bytes `7b22610962223a20317d`, the character raw | `22P02`, `0x09` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `["a<01>b"]`, an array element | bytes `5b22615c753030303162225d`, written back as a `\u` escape | `22P02`, `0x01` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `"a<TAB>b"`, a scalar string | bytes `22615c746222`, written back as its escape | `22P02`, `0x09` | answers |
  | simple `Query` `INSERT INTO r136 VALUES (1, '…')`, `v jsonb` | `{"k": "a<01>b"}` | `INSERT 0 1`; `v::text` reads back `7b226b223a2022615c753030303162227d` | `22P02`, `0x01`, no row | writes |
  | simple `Query` `INSERT INTO r136 VALUES (2, '…')`, `v jsonb` | `{"k": "a<TAB>b"}` | `INSERT 0 1`; `v::text` reads back `7b226b223a2022615c7462227d` | `22P02`, `0x09`, no row | writes |
  | `Parse`, `Bind`, `Execute` of `SELECT $1::jsonb::text`, `$1` in text format | `{"k": "a<01>b"}` | a row, bytes `7b226b223a2022615c753030303162227d` | `22P02`, `0x01` | answers |
  | `Parse`, `Bind`, `Execute` of `SELECT $1::jsonb::text`, `$1` in text format | `{"k": "a<1F>b"}` | a row, bytes `7b226b223a2022615c753030316662227d` | `22P02`, `0x1f` | answers |
  | `Parse`, `Bind`, `Execute` of `INSERT INTO r136 VALUES ($1, $2)`, `$2` untyped in text format | `{"k": "a<TAB>b"}` | `INSERT 0 1`; `v::text` reads back `7b226b223a2022615c7462227d` | `22P02`, `0x09`, no row | writes |
  | `COPY r136c FROM STDIN`, text format, `v jsonb` the second field | `{"k": "a<01>b"}` | `COPY 1`; `v::text` reads back `7b226b223a2022615c753030303162227d` | `22P02`, `0x01`, no row | writes |
  | `COPY r136c FROM STDIN`, text format, `v jsonb` the second field | `{"a<1F>b": 1}`, an object key | `COPY 1`; `v::text` reads back `7b22611f62223a20317d`, the character raw | `22P02`, `0x1f`, no row | writes |

  On this build every member above answers `22P02 invalid input syntax for type json`,
  matching 18.6's SQLSTATE at each, and the `INSERT` and `COPY` members leave no row —
  re-measured over the same raw wire client at each input in the table. What pglet does
  not send with it is 18.6's `D` (`Character with value 0x… must be escaped.`), `P` and
  `W`: row 76's standing omission, which `ErrorFields::divergences` scores as agreement.

  Controls agreeing on both engines: `{"k": "a<7F>b"}`, `<7F>` standing for `0x7F`, which is
  above the `31` 18.6's lexer tests, answers bytes `7b226b223a2022617f62227d` on both; a tab
  outside any string, `{"k":<TAB>1}`, is JSON whitespace and answers `{"k": 1}` on both; the
  escaped spelling `{"k": "a\tb"}` answers `7b226b223a2022615c7462227d` on both; and
  `{"k": "ab"}` answers on both through the cast, the simple-`Query` `INSERT`, the `$1` cast
  and `COPY`, reading back `7b226b223a20226162227d`.

  A NUL is not a member of this code. At a text-format `$1` and in a `COPY` line,
  `{"k": "a<00>b"}`, `<00>` standing for `0x00`, is
  `22021 invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00` on both engines, with no row —
  18.6 raising it from its encoding check, which answers ahead of its JSON lexer, and
  pglet from the scan that check's counterpart reaches (`docs/encoding.md` § The doors
  that reach it). The reader has a `22021` arm of its own for a *raw* NUL inside a JSON
  string, and **18.6's JSON lexer has no counterpart to it**: that arm exists for the
  routes that reach the reader having skipped the scan, which are the in-process doors of
  row 133, so the code it answers is the one the two engines were measured to agree on at
  the routes above rather than the `22P02` its neighbouring control characters take.
  Row 133 records what a NUL taken through an in-process door costs.

  Row 135's bullet records a dump of an object key holding a tab, whose `COPY` line `COPY`
  read back as a raw tab inside the key: it restored into pglet, through this reader, and
  not into 18.6. That shape is unreachable now — the line cannot be written and the reader
  would refuse it either way.

  What pins it: the `jsonb/raw_control_*` fixtures — a tab at a value and at a key, `0x01`
  in an array element, `0x1F` in a scalar string, and `raw_control_boundary_accepted.sql`
  for both ends of the range, where a space and `0x7F` must still be taken — plus the two
  precedence pairs, each written from both sides:
  `raw_control_outranks_a_later_escape_zero.sql` against
  `escape_zero_outranks_a_later_raw_control.sql`, and
  `raw_control_outranks_a_later_number_range.sql` against
  `number_range_outranks_a_later_raw_control.sql`;
  `jsonb/escaped_control_accepted.sql` for the decoded-versus-raw distinction,
  `jsonb/default_raw_control_loud.sql` for the DDL position whose acceptance used to brick
  a dump, `copy/jsonb_raw_control_from_loud.sql` for the field `CopyReadAttributesText`
  de-escapes into a raw tab, `json.rs`'s reader tests, and
  `crates/pglet/tests/jsonb_reader_doors.rs` for the in-process doors no fixture can
  reach.

- **~~137~~ · Closed — whitespace 18.6's JSON lexer does not skip.** pglet's jsonb reader
  (`pglet_core::types::json`) dropped the whitespace around a value, a key, a colon and a
  container's body with Rust's `str::trim` and `trim_start`, called in `parse_json_at`,
  `parse_json_object`, `parse_json_pair` and `parse_json_array`; those strip characters
  carrying the Unicode `White_Space` property. 18.6's `json_lex` (`src/common/jsonapi.c`)
  skips only space, tab, LF and CR ahead of a token, so another `White_Space` character
  standing there is read as the start of a token, and the input is
  `22P02 invalid input syntax for type json` with the detail `Token "…" is invalid.`
  Each of those calls is `json_trim` or `json_trim_start` now — `str::trim` narrowed to
  `is_json_whitespace`, which is those four characters and nothing else.

  **What it cost.** At a position one of those calls trimmed, pglet dropped a
  `White_Space` character that 18.6 reads as an invalid token, so a statement that read
  such text answered or wrote with no error, and the value held no trace of the character.

  The members measured **before the repair**, over a raw wire client on both engines,
  `<0B>` and `<0C>` standing for the bytes `0x0B` and `0x0C`, and `<U+0085>`, `<U+00A0>`,
  `<U+2028>` and `<U+3000>` for those characters in UTF-8. Each 18.6 answer is
  `22P02 invalid input syntax for type json` with the detail `Token "…" is invalid.`, and
  where the table says *no row* none was stored. They are what was measured, not a closed
  set:

  | route | input | pglet before | 18.6 | here, before |

  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `{"k":<0C>1}`, after a colon | `{"k": 1}` | `22P02` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `{"k":<0B>1}`, after a colon | `{"k": 1}` | `22P02` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `{"k"<0B>:1}`, between a key and its colon | `{"k": 1}` | `22P02` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `<0C>1`, before a top-level number | `1` | `22P02` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `1<0B>`, after a top-level number | `1` | `22P02` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `<U+0085>1`, before a top-level number | `1` | `22P02` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `1<U+00A0>`, after a top-level number | `1` | `22P02` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `1<U+3000>`, after a top-level number | `1` | `22P02` | answers |
  | `SELECT '…'::jsonb::text` | `<U+3000>"a"`, before a top-level string | `"a"` | `22P02` | answers |

  | simple `Query` `INSERT INTO r137 VALUES (1, '…')`, `v jsonb` | `{"k":<0C>1}` | `INSERT 0 1`; `v::text` reads back `{"k": 1}` | `22P02`, no row | writes |
  | `Parse`, `Bind`, `Execute` of `SELECT $1::jsonb::text`, `$1` in text format | `<U+0085>1` | a row, `1` | `22P02` | answers |
  | `Parse`, `Bind`, `Execute` of `INSERT INTO r137 VALUES ($1, $2)`, `$2` untyped in text format | `1<0B>` | `INSERT 0 1`; `v::text` reads back `1` | `22P02`, no row | writes |

  On this build every member above answers `22P02 invalid input syntax for type json`,
  matching 18.6's SQLSTATE at each, and the `INSERT` and `COPY` members leave no row —
  re-measured over the same raw wire client at each input in the table. The `D`

  76's standing omission, which `ErrorFields::divergences` scores as agreement.

  its colon, before an object key, before an array element, after an array comma, before
  and after a top-level token, and as the whole body of an empty object and of an empty
